The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge2$. A fixed massive rest representation fiber consists here of a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, a number $M>0$ with $P^0=MI$ and $P^j=0$, and scalar central charges $Z^{IJ}=z^{IJ}I$, where $Z=(z^{IJ})$ is the complex antisymmetric $N\times N$ matrix in the four-dimensional algebra with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\epsilon_{12}=1$. Suppose the charge operators and their actual Hilbert adjoints have a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$ on the fiber and every product in the expanded anticommutators is defined there. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $M$ and each $z^{IJ}$ have mass dimension one. For $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_N)\in\mathbb C^N$ define $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_I|v_I|^2$ and for $u,v\in\mathbb C^N$ put $u^*Zv=\sum_{I,J}\bar u_Iz^{IJ}v_J$. Define

$$\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Zv\|_2.$$

Then $M\ge\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. For $N=2$, write $z=z^{12}$, so $Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|z|$. If $z\ne0$, set $\omega=z/|z|$; if $z=0$, set $\omega=1$. Then $|\omega|=1$ and $\overline\omega z=|z|$, as verified in the proof below. Define on $\mathcal D$

$$A:=Q^1_1-\omega(Q^2_2)^*,\qquad A^\sharp:=(Q^1_1)^*-\overline\omega Q^2_2.$$

The algebraic anticommutator $AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A$ equals $4(M-|z|)I$ on $\mathcal D$. Here $A^\sharp$ is the displayed combination of the individual actual adjoints; it is not asserted to be the adjoint of an unbounded sum on its maximal domain. If $\mathcal K$ is finite-dimensional, all charge domains equal $\mathcal K$ and $A^\sharp=A^*$, so the formula is the ordinary operator anticommutator. At saturation $M=|z|$, for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ one has $A\psi=A^\sharp\psi=0$. This is a representation-theoretic fiber statement: it does not assert that the fixed-momentum fiber is a normalizable subspace of the full Hilbert space, or that a state with specified charge exists or is stable.

For each $I,\alpha$, the supercharge $Q^I_\alpha$ is a closed densely defined operator on $\mathcal H$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}=(Q^I_\alpha)^*$ is its actual Hilbert adjoint, with exactly the adjoint domain. Require the grading to preserve each actual charge domain and each closed charge to be odd there: $\Gamma D(Q^I_\alpha)=D(Q^I_\alpha)$ and $Q^I_\alpha\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma Q^I_\alpha\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q^I_\alpha)$, with the same two conditions for $(Q^I_\alpha)^*$ on $D((Q^I_\alpha)^*)$. The central generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}$, which belong to the even part of the algebra, are represented by closed densely defined operators with $\bar Z_{IJ}=(Z^{IJ})^*$ as an actual Hilbert adjoint; require $\Gamma D(Z^{IJ})=D(Z^{IJ})$ and $Z^{IJ}\Gamma\psi=\Gamma Z^{IJ}\psi$ on $D(Z^{IJ})$, with the corresponding conditions for $\bar Z_{IJ}$ on its actual domain. On a common dense graded linear domain $\mathcal D$, contained in the domains of every generator product in the bracket table, the operator supercommutator is the displayed algebra bracket. $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a selected pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills model whose global gauge group is $SU(2)$.
The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty, as explicitly adopted in the independent pure-model postulate. In $\mathcal N=1$ language the gauge sector is one vector superfield and one adjoint chiral superfield with scalar $\phi\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, connection normalization $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$, positive dimensionless gauge coupling $g$, zero chiral superpotential and no ultraviolet matter mass. A **classical Coulomb-branch configuration** is a constant adjoint scalar
configuration satisfying the model's zero auxiliary-field conditions, taken
modulo the compact $SU(2)$ gauge action. This uses the compact-group orbit
quotient in the preceding vacuum-moduli definition; it does not replace that
quotient by a complexified-group stability construction. In the
weak-coupling semiclassical frame, let $a_{\mathrm{cl}}$ be the eigenvalue coordinate fixed
by $\phi=\tfrac12\operatorname{diag}(a_{\mathrm{cl}},-a_{\mathrm{cl}})$, of mass dimension one. When a quantum
theory with a vacuum-moduli set has actually been constructed, the **quantum
Coulomb-branch coordinate** $u$ denotes the chosen gauge-invariant chiral
quadratic-operator expectation value in the source trace normalization for
which the classical relation is $u_{\mathrm{cl}}=a_{\mathrm{cl}}^2/2$.
Here $a_{\mathrm{cl}}$ denotes the preceding classical eigenvalue coordinate;
the quantum $a(u)$ below is a local period, with weak-coupling normalization
$a(u)^2/(2u)\to1$ as $|u|/\Lambda^2\to\infty$ on a chosen electric branch,
where $\Lambda>0$ is the fixed dynamical scale of mass dimension one.
This is an asymptotic relation, not an identity at finite quantum $u$.
The mass dimension of $u$ is two.
This definition does not assert that $u$ globally parameterizes the quantum

Equip the **formal electric/magnetic charge lattice**
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$ with the alternating integer-valued form
$\omega_\Gamma((n_e,n_m),(k_e,k_m))=n_mk_e-n_ek_m$ in its reference coordinates.
This form fixes an orientation convention for frames; it does not specify
the normalization of a physical Dirac pairing. An **electric/magnetic
frame** is an ordered lattice basis $(\gamma_m,\gamma_e)$ satisfying
$\omega_\Gamma(\gamma_m,\gamma_e)=1$, called a symplectic basis here. When realized
by homology cycles, its intersection convention is
$\gamma_m\mathbin{\cdot}\gamma_e=1$.

On a sufficiently small open regular patch $U$ of the $u$-plane, supply
holomorphic period functions $a_D,a:U\to\mathbb C$ for these magnetic and
electric basis elements, both of mass dimension one. Require $a$ to be a
holomorphic coordinate on $U$, with $da/du\ne0$, and require the local
coupling below to have positive imaginary part. The local
two-derivative abelian gauge action is encoded by a holomorphic
**prepotential** $\mathcal F_U:a(U)\to\mathbb C$ of mass dimension two,
defined in this coordinate by

$$a_D=\frac{\partial\mathcal F_U}{\partial a},\qquad \tau=\frac{\partial a_D}{\partial a}=\frac{\partial^2\mathcal F_U}{\partial a^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0.$$

The dimensionless $\tau$ is the local complexified gauge coupling. A frame
change on a connected overlap has a constant matrix
$M=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\r&s\end{pmatrix}\in SL(2,\mathbb Z)$, meaning
$p,q,r,s\in\mathbb Z$ and $ps-qr=1$, and acts by

$$\begin{pmatrix}\widetilde\gamma_m\\\widetilde\gamma_e\end{pmatrix}=M\begin{pmatrix}\gamma_m\\\gamma_e\end{pmatrix},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}\widetilde a_D\\\widetilde a\end{pmatrix}=M\begin{pmatrix}a_D\\a\end{pmatrix},\qquad \widetilde\tau=\frac{p\tau+q}{r\tau+s}.$$

After shrinking the overlap if necessary, use a local prepotential in the
new electric coordinate $\widetilde a$. No determinant-minus-one change is
a frame change in this convention. Neither period is asserted to be a
single-valued global function on a punctured branch.

In the selected frame, the **formal electric/magnetic charge label**
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$ represents
$\gamma=n_e\gamma_e+n_m\gamma_m$, with period pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The pair labels
the central-charge formula; the lattice definition does not assert that every
label is an allowed line operator, a dynamical particle, a stable state, or a
state in any constructed Hilbert space. Those are separate model data.
For the same $\gamma$ in the changed frame the charge row transforms by
$(\widetilde n_m,\widetilde n_e)=(n_m,n_e)M^{-1}$, so the period pairing
is unchanged.

The word **exact** in this page refers only to the adopted source-proposed
Wilsonian two-derivative low-energy data on a regular patch of the selected
pure SU(2) model. It does not mean a proof of a nonperturbative continuum
path integral, a global single-valued prepotential, or an exact statement

rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills with global gauge group $SU(2)$, one
adjoint vector multiplet, rank one, no matter hypermultiplets, and the coupling, units, connection-normalized scalar, and prepotential convention of the independent pure ultraviolet vector-multiplet datum. On the regular $w$-plane with singular values $w=1,-1,\infty$ removed,
adopt the family of genus-one curves, where $x,y,w$ are dimensionless:

$$\Sigma_w:\quad y^2=(x-1)(x+1)(x-w).$$

and the meromorphic period differential

$$\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}=\frac{\sqrt2\Lambda}{2\pi}\frac{y\,dx}{x^2-1}.$$

Within this proposed solution, take the quantum vacuum-moduli data to be the

values $u=\Lambda^2,-\Lambda^2,\infty$. This is part of the adopted

For a chosen local cycle basis $\gamma_m,\gamma_e$ on $\Sigma_w$ with

$a_D=\partial\mathcal F/\partial a$ and

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ write the smooth one-form
$\widetilde A=\widetilde A_r\,dr+\widetilde A_\theta\,d\theta$.
For a disk of radius $R$, integration of
$\widetilde F_{r\theta}=\partial_r\widetilde A_\theta-
\partial_\theta\widetilde A_r$ first in $r$ and then in $\theta$ gives
$\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x
=\int_0^{2\pi}\widetilde A_\theta(R,\theta)\,d\theta$: the
$\theta$-derivative term cancels by single-valuedness, and the inner
boundary term tends to zero because a smooth one-form has
$\widetilde A_\theta=O(r)$ at the origin.

On a sufficiently large circle choose a continuous phase
$M/|M|=e^{i\vartheta(\theta)}$ with
$\vartheta(2\pi)-\vartheta(0)=2\pi n$. The tangential condition in [F1]
implies $\widetilde A_\theta(R,\theta)-
\partial_\theta\vartheta(\theta)\to0$ uniformly in $\theta$ as
$R\to\infty$.
Taking the limit in step 1.1 therefore gives
$\Phi_D=\int_0^{2\pi}\partial_\theta\vartheta\,d\theta=2\pi n$.

Since $n\ne0$, step 2.1 gives nonzero flux, so the smooth function
$\widetilde F_{12}$ is nonzero at some point and hence on a neighborhood of
that point. Its squared integral is strictly positive. By [F2] and
$g_D>0$, the Maxwell term contributes strictly positive energy, while all
remaining energy terms are nonnegative; thus $\sigma>0$. Finiteness of
$\sigma$ is part of [F1]'s admitted-profile hypothesis.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Use the local monopole fields, charges and superpotential with $a=A_D$, $c=u'(0)\ne0$, $\mu\ne0$, $v^2=|\mu c|/\sqrt2$ and $\xi=2v^2$. Keep the holomorphic function $u$ nonlinear. Choose a closed disk $K_\delta=\{|a|\le\delta\}$ contained in its open valid patch with $u'(a)\ne0$ throughout. Define

$$m_*=\min_{a\in K_\delta}|\mu u'(a)|>0,\qquad K=\sup_{a\in K_\delta}|\mu u''(a)|<\infty.$$

Continuity, compactness and the nonzero $c$ allow such a disk. No linear Taylor replacement of $u$ is made. In the already adopted constant-metric model put $b(a)=b_0=g_D^{-2}$. More generally, the same classical energy problem may be specified with a supplied smooth real function $b$ on a neighborhood of $K_\delta$ and constants $0<b_-\le b(a)\le b_+<\infty$. This is additional explicit local Wilsonian metric data, not the vector-only logarithmically singular period metric inferred at a massless-monopole point. Let $b_0=b(0)$ and $g_0^2=b_0^{-1}$. Define

$$H=\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu u'(a),\qquad d=|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2,\qquad s=|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2,$$

$$V_b=b(a)^{-1}|H|^2+\frac{d^2}{2b(a)}+2|a|^2s.$$

Charged kinetic terms are canonical. The gauge kinetic coefficient is $b(a)$ and the neutral kinetic coefficient is $b(a)$. Work in the classical magnetostatic model with omitted or **constant** theta angle, no dynamical dual magnetic sources in the interior, static fields and $A_0=0$. No field-dependent-theta Gauss-law conclusion is included.

Fix $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ and $e^{i\beta}=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v^2)$. A planar admissible profile is a smooth real one-form $A=A_1dx^1+A_2dx^2$ and smooth complex fields $a,M,\widetilde M$ on $\mathbb R^2$, with $a(x)\in K_\delta$, finite energy

$$E_b=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{b(a)}2B^2+b(a)|\partial_i a|^2+|D_iM|^2+|\widetilde D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_b\right\}d^2x,$$

where $i=1,2$, $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, $D_i=\partial_i-iA_i$ and $\widetilde D_i=\partial_i+iA_i$. Require **uniform** approach to the vacuum orbit at transverse infinity:

$$a\to0,\qquad |M|,|\widetilde M|\to v,\qquad M\widetilde M\to e^{i\beta}v^2.$$

This is an independent boundary hypothesis, not inferred from finite energy. Outside a compact set $M$ is nonzero and its phase has winding $n$ on each sufficiently large circle; the phase of $\widetilde M$ has winding $-n$. In the angular coordinate $\theta$, require the coefficient of $d\theta$ in $A-d\arg M$ to tend uniformly to zero, and the limiting flux to exist. Require also $D_iM,\widetilde D_i\widetilde M\to0$ uniformly, as in the admitted flux-sector data. These conditions define the gauge-invariant class $\mathcal P_n$. Gauge transformations are arbitrary smooth maps $U:\mathbb R^2\to U(1)$ acting by $M\mapsto UM$, $\widetilde M\mapsto U^{-1}\widetilde M$ and $A\mapsto A-iU^{-1}dU$; there is no added asymptotic-constant gauge restriction. A **canonical exterior representative** has $M=m e^{in\theta}$ with $m>0$ real outside a compact set.

Write

$$\tau_n=\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_b(P).$$

This notation alone asserts neither nonemptiness nor attainment. The adopted electric/magnetic dictionary identifies the dual magnetic flux with the original electric flux only for the specified test-charge/flux boundary sector.

For fixed canonical exterior representatives $P_0,P_1\in\mathcal P_n$ and $L>0$, use coordinates $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ and write the cylinder gauge potential as $\mathcal A=A_1dx^1+A_2dx^2+A_3dx^3$. Define $F=d\mathcal A$, so $F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i$ for $1\le i,j\le3$, and extend the charged covariant derivatives by $D_i=\partial_i-iA_i$ and $\widetilde D_i=\partial_i+iA_i$ for $i=1,2,3$. The tangential end traces are $(A_1dx^1+A_2dx^2,a,M,\widetilde M)$ at $x^3=0,L$; no endpoint value is prescribed for the normal component $A_3$. Let $\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)$ be the smooth static fields on $\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ with these end traces, $a\in K_\delta$, and a planar admissible winding-$n$ profile on almost every slice. The flux $2\pi n$ is thus fixed throughout the cylinder, with no flux leakage to transverse infinity or interior magnetic source. Allow $A_3$ but choose $A_3=0$ in trial collars. Define

$$E_{b,3}=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{b(a)}2\sum_{i<j}F_{ij}^2+b(a)\sum_{i=1}^3|\partial_i a|^2+\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(|D_iM|^2+|\widetilde D_i\widetilde M|^2\bigr)+V_b\right\}d^2x\,dx^3,$$

and $I_n(L;P_0,P_1)=\inf_{\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)}E_{b,3}$. Competitors have finite displayed energy and the stated flux/boundary data; no stationary solution or minimizer is assumed. Any further hard field cutoff is part of a different admissible class and must be checked to admit the profiles and interpolation paths used here. This functional is the specified local classical model; no error control to a microscopic action or quantum Wilson-loop interpretation is asserted.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be an oriented smooth $n$-manifold with boundary, $n\geq1$, and let $\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)$. With $j:\partial M\hookrightarrow M$ and the outward-normal-first orientation,
$$\int_M d\eta=\int_{\partial M}j^*\eta.$$
An empty boundary contributes zero; in dimension one its integral is a finite signed sum of point values.

If $f,g\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, then

$$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $f,g$ is zero almost everywhere,
or there is a constant $c>0$ with

$$|f|^2=c\,|g|^2\qquad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

derivations.claim: Put $x=\sqrt2M\widetilde M$ and $U_0=\mu c$, so $s^2=d^2+2|x|^2$ and $\xi=\sqrt2|U_0|$. By the fundamental theorem of calculus along the segment from $0$ to $a$ inside the convex disk, $|\mu(u'(a)-c)|\le K|a|$. If $s\le t_*$, then $|x|\le s/\sqrt2\le m_*/2$, whereas the disk hypothesis gives $|\mu u'(a)|\ge m_*$. Hence $|H|\ge m_*/2$ and $V_b\ge m_*^2/(4b_+)\ge[m_*^2/(4b_+\xi^2)](s-\xi)^2$, since $s\le t_*\le\xi/2$. If $s\ge t_*$, give $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb C$ the norm $\|(r,z)\|^2=r^2+|z|^2$ and use the reverse triangle inequality $|\|v\|-\|w\||\le\|v-w\|$ with $v=(d,\sqrt2x)$ and $w=(0,-\sqrt2U_0)$. It gives $(s-\xi)^2\le d^2+2|x+U_0|^2$. Set $\delta=\mu(u'(a)-c)$; then $x+U_0=H-\delta$, and $|x+U_0|^2\le2|H|^2+2K^2|a|^2$. Consequently $(s-\xi)^2\le d^2+4|H|^2+4K^2|a|^2$. The three terms are bounded by $2b_+V_b$, $4b_+V_b$, and $2K^2V_b/t_*$, respectively, because $V_b\ge2|a|^2s\ge2t_*|a|^2$. Combining the cases proves the stated uniform potential bound without a Hessian or minimizer assumption.

Use the unitary real-linear change $q=(M+e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M})/\sqrt2$, $p=(M-e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M})/\sqrt2$; both fields have charge +1 and $s=|q|^2+|p|^2$. Their summed covariant-gradient norms equal the original charged norms. Let $E_0$ be the critical two-charge functional with terms $b_0B^2/2+|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2+(s-\xi)^2/(2b_0)$ and no additional p-mass term. The Maxwell bound $b\ge b_-$, step 1.1 and the definition of $\gamma$ give $E_b\ge\gamma E_0$, after dropping the nonnegative neutral gradient. In particular $E_0$ is finite. Uniform vacuum approach makes q,p bounded near infinity, with $|q|\to\sqrt\xi$ and $p\to0$ in the vacuum phase frame. Stokes on disks and the original angular condition give limiting flux $2\pi n$.

Write $G(R)=\int_{|x|=R}(|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2)\,ds$. Finiteness of the gradient integral implies $\int_{R_0}^{\infty}G(R)\,dR<\infty$. There are radii $R_j\to\infty$ with $R_jG(R_j)\to0$: otherwise $G(R)\ge\epsilon/R$ eventually for some $\epsilon>0$, contradicting that integral. By [F3] and bounded tail amplitudes, the absolute boundary-current integral $\oint(\bar qDq+\bar pDp)$ on these circles is at most $C\sqrt{R_jG(R_j)}\to0$. For $n>0$, expand the disk square identity using $[D_1,D_2]f=-iBf$ for $f=q,p$: $|(D_1+iD_2)f|^2=|Df|^2-B|f|^2+i\{\partial_1(\bar fD_2f)-\partial_2(\bar fD_1f)\}$ and $b_0[B-b_0^{-1}(\xi-s)]^2/2=b_0B^2/2+(s-\xi)^2/(2b_0)+Bs-\xi B$. Add the identities, integrate, and let $R_j\to\infty$. The boundary current vanishes along this subsequence, the flux tends to $2\pi n$ and the remaining squares are nonnegative, so $E_0\ge2\pi\xi n$. Reflection of the second transverse coordinate proves $E_0\ge2\pi\xi|n|$ for negative n. Step 2.1 now proves the claimed positive bound for every full-model profile. No full-circle boundary-current limit was assumed or inferred from finite energy.

Let $N=|n|$. Choose smooth radial functions f,h with f(r) equal to a positive constant times $r^N$ near zero, h(r) equal to a constant times $r^2$ near zero, and $f=h=1$ outside one fixed disk; choose the near-zero coefficients as smooth functions of $r^2$ and interpolate on a compact annulus. Set $q=\sqrt\xi f(r)e^{in\theta}$, $p=a=0$, and $A=nh(r)d\theta$, hence $M=q/\sqrt2$, $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}\bar q/\sqrt2$. The charged fields are smooth at zero because $r^Ne^{in\theta}$ is $z^N$ or $\bar z^N$, and the connection is smooth because $r^2d\theta=x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1$. Curvature and every non-vacuum energy term are supported in a fixed disk; all are smooth there. Outside it the field is exactly in the vacuum orbit, the covariant gradients vanish and the angular flux coefficient is n. Thus this is an admitted finite-energy profile. Its energy is positive by step 3.1 and finite directly; consequently $0<\gamma2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty$.

For any profile, M is nonzero outside a disk by uniform vacuum approach. The circle-valued function $(M/|M|)e^{-in\theta}$ has degree zero on that exterior annulus. It has a smooth real phase lift $\chi$: the closed real one-form $-if^{-1}df$ for this circle-valued function f has zero integral on each circle, so integrating first radially and then angularly from a fixed base point defines a smooth periodic lift with $e^{i\chi}=f$. Multiply $-\chi$ by a radial smooth cutoff equal to zero near the inner boundary and one on a larger exterior annulus, then exponentiate to obtain a globally smooth gauge transformation. The transformed fields have $M=m e^{in\theta}$, $m>0$, and $A=nd\theta+\alpha$ outside a compact set. This gauge change leaves energy and the original angular condition invariant and fixes the exact exterior M-phase; it does not impose a new decay hypothesis. Write $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}w e^{-in\theta}$, so m,w tend uniformly to v.

On this exterior, s is bounded below by $\xi/2$ and m by $v/2$. The potential controls $|a|^2\le V_b/\xi$, $d^2\le2b_+V_b$, $|H|^2\le b_+V_b$ and $(s-\xi)^2\le C_VV_b$. Since $m^2-v^2=(s+d-\xi)/2$, $|m-v|^2\le[(s-\xi)^2+d^2]/(2v^2)$ is integrable. Also $m w-v^2=e^{-i\beta}[H-\mu(u'(a)-c)]/\sqrt2$, so $|w-v|\le(2/v)\{(|H|+K|a|)/\sqrt2+v|m-v|\}$ is square-integrable. Thus a,m-v,w-v are in $L^2$ on the exterior. Finally $DM=e^{in\theta}(dm-im\alpha)$, with dm and alpha real. Its squared norm is $|dm|^2+m^2|\alpha|^2$, so finite charged energy and $m\ge v/2$ give $\alpha,dm\in L^2$. On compact sets all fields and coefficients are smooth and bounded. Hence any two canonical profiles differ in $L^2$ in a,M,$\widetilde M$ and their connection one-forms. These mass-tail conclusions use uniform approach to the vacuum as well as the finite potential/kinetic energy; finite energy alone was not asserted to force pointwise vacuum approach.

Let two canonical profiles be given and choose one radius beyond both cleanup disks. A smooth cutoff $\eta(t)$, t in [0,ell], constant zero near 0 and one near ell, defines an explicit collar by linearly blending a,M,$\widetilde M$,$A_1,A_2$ and setting $A_3=0$. The neutral disk is convex, so the blend stays in it. Longitudinal scalar derivatives and $F_{3i}$ are $\eta'$ times the corresponding $L^2$ differences from step 6.1, hence have finite energy. For either charged field f, its transverse covariant derivative along the blend equals the blend of the two original covariant derivatives plus a bounded coefficient times $(A^{(1)}-A^{(0)})(f^{(1)}-f^{(0)})$. The connection difference is $L^2$ and the field difference is bounded globally, so this term is $L^2$; neutral gradients and transverse curvatures also blend linearly. Near infinity the field deviations from the common canonical vacuum frame are $L^2$ and uniformly small. Smoothness of u,b and vanishing of the potential and its first derivatives on that vacuum orbit give the uniform local estimate $V_b\le C(|a|^2+|m-v|^2+|w-v|^2)$ along the blend, by a Taylor formula on one compact transverse slice of the phase orbit. This makes the collar potential integrable; compact interiors have finite energy by smoothness. The exterior M-phase remains exactly $e^{in\theta}$ because its blended amplitude is positive, and $A_\theta-n$ is a convex blend of two functions tending uniformly to zero. Thus winding, angular condition and limiting flux are preserved on every collar slice; uniform covariant-gradient decay is preserved by the same product formula, using $\alpha\to0$ from $DM\to0$ and $m\ge v/2$. This constructs an actual finite-energy collar, with cost independent of any later cylinder length L.

The three-dimensional energy is the transverse planar energy on each slice plus nonnegative longitudinal Maxwell and scalar terms. By [F4] and the definition of $\tau_n$, every competitor has $E_{b,3}\ge\tau_nL$. For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the definition of the finite infimum provides one planar profile with energy below $\tau_n+\varepsilon$; gauge-clean it by step 5.1. Step 7.1 constructs collars from each fixed end trace to this profile, with one chosen width ell and finite total energy $C_\varepsilon$, independent of L. Concatenate the collars with its translation-invariant extension over length L-2ell. This is a smooth admissible competitor because each collar is constant near the inner face, and it has energy at most $(\tau_n+\varepsilon)(L-2\ell)+C_\varepsilon$. Taking the infimum proves the two-sided bounds. Dividing by L, taking limsup as L tends to infinity and then allowing each $\varepsilon>0$ to tend to zero gives $\limsup\le\tau_n$, while the lower bound gives $\liminf\ge\tau_n$. Hence the limit is $\tau_n>0$. No minimizer or uniform bound on $C_\varepsilon$ as epsilon tends to zero is used, so no generic $O(1)$ remainder follows.

With constant or absent theta, the Gauss constraint is therefore zero on every constructed trial field, including collars, even when b varies spatially.
